wording: One pinned toolchain builds an Anchor program that uses MagicBlock delegation, commit intents, Magic Actions, PER access control, and crank scheduling together.
limitations: Compilation and SBF linking only. No instruction was executed on any runtime.
The probe holds no VINCT product logic and is never deployed.
Says nothing about delegation, PER confidentiality, crank execution, or Magic Action delivery behaviour.

wording: The MagicBlock development skill, the Solana development skill, and the MagicBlock engine examples are pinned to exact upstream commits resolved during this phase.
limitations: Commits were HEAD of each default branch on 2026-08-07 and will drift.
The engine examples are inspected out-of-tree, not vendored, so the pin is a recorded SHA rather than a checked-in tree.

wording: The pinned local MagicBlock stack starts, answers getHealth on its base, ephemeral, and query-filtering endpoints, and stops leaving no surviving process.
limitations: Process lifecycle and RPC health only. No account was created, delegated, or committed.
Does not prove router discovery, TEE-backed PER confidentiality, crank registration, or Magic Action delivery.
Requires a locally patched validator-identity fixture because the packaged dump funds the ephemeral validator below its 5 SOL minimum.

wording: MagicBlock devnet service status was captured from the official status API with a timestamp, including one service reported down.
limitations: A snapshot of one moment. Service health must be re-captured before every rehearsal.
rpc_router on devnet-tee-as.magicblock.app was DOWN at capture time.
Reports the provider's own status, which is not independent verification of the services.

wording: The MagicBlock devnet router's advertised endpoints were read live, and no regional endpoint is hardcoded in this repository.
limitations: getDelegationStatus was probed with an undelegated account and returned only {isDelegated:false}.
Whether a delegated account's response carries an fqdn is UNVERIFIED. The PRD's endpoint-resolution instruction is not yet confirmed.
No account was delegated, so no ER endpoint was actually resolved or used.

wording: The ephemeral-rollups-sdk anchor feature line was chosen against a failing counterexample rather than from documentation alone.
commands: cargo check (probe source rebuilt with the anchor-compat feature)
limitations: The counterexample crate is a scratch build and is not committed to this repository.
A stub crate declaring anchor-compat alongside anchor-lang 1.0.2 still passes cargo check, so this result depends on exercising the macros.

wording: One pure Rust reference model defines every VINCT covenant, incident, certificate, settlement, and recovery rule, and no expected value is implemented a second time.
limitations: Deterministic model only. No account constraint, no runtime, no network behaviour is proven here.
The model takes resolved addresses as input; it does not derive program addresses, which needs a Solana runtime.

wording: Every one-byte and one-order mutation the PRD enumerates either changes the canonical digest or is rejected outright, including sorting account metas.
limitations: Covers the canonical encoding only. An on-chain program that fails to feed the right bytes into these types is a separate risk, addressed from Phase 2.
26 mutation vectors are committed; 22 produce distinct digests and 4 are rejected before hashing.

wording: All 1024 states of the three-member covenant were enumerated, and certification never occurs without the frozen threshold being met.
limitations: Exhaustive for three members, one threshold, and one ceiling. Larger covenants are covered by property tests, not enumeration.
Enumerates evaluation outcomes, not on-chain instruction behaviour.

wording: Quarantine can never cause a certification, in any state of the three-member covenant or under property testing up to eight members.
limitations: A property test found the original implementation violating this. The claim describes the corrected model, recorded as D-0013.
Assumes the quarantine authority cannot also forge attestations; that is a separate control tested from Phase 4.

wording: The operation identity is computable before any concrete action bundle exists, every one of its eight inputs is load-bearing, and the concrete bundle stays cryptographically bound through the certificate.
limitations: Corrects PRD sections 12.3 and 12.4, whose derivation was circular and could not be implemented. Recorded as D-0012.
Replay resistance is proven against the model's capability-bounds check, not yet against a deployed adapter program.

wording: An independently written TypeScript encoder reproduces every canonical Borsh preimage and SHA-256 digest byte for byte.
limitations: The TypeScript side implements Borsh from the specification rather than reusing the Rust encoder, which is what makes the check independent.
Rust remains authoritative. The vectors prove agreement, not that either implementation is correct in isolation.
17 negative tests confirm the parity checker reports disagreement when one is introduced.

wording: Settlement reaches SETTLED only when every adapter receipt, every target effect, and the final settlement receipt were positively observed, and an unreadable observation is never treated as absence.
limitations: Classifies supplied observations. Whether the observations themselves are complete depends on the Phase 3 reconciler.
The real committor's transaction-strategy grouping is still unmeasured, so which classifications actually occur on Devnet is unknown until Phase 3.

wording: Three reference protocols hold genuinely separate authorities, and each one registers its own adapter signer that no other protocol, the steward, or the circle can install.
limitations: In-process SVM. Proves account and authority constraints, not delegation, PER, cranks, or Magic Action delivery.
The three protocols share one program binary the way three real protocols would share a forked codebase; they share no authority.
The protocols are reference fixtures, not real deployed protocols.

wording: The sovereign adapter exposes no path that forwards a caller-supplied program, discriminator, account list, or instruction data, and every capability field is enforced against a named error.
limitations: The adapter does not verify the whole-cohort action bundle hash; that binding lives on the certificate and in the standalone verifier. See docs/decision-log.md D-0019.
Adversarial coverage is over the instruction surface as built. A program upgrade needs the suite re-run.
39 adversarial cases cover certificate bindings, capability fields, account substitution, and replay.

wording: An operation cannot be executed twice: the adapter refuses it, and the target protocol independently refuses it even if the adapter were bypassed.
limitations: Idempotency is per operation ID. A recovery operation deliberately carries a new one and is therefore executable, which is the intended behaviour.
The market's own record holds only the last operation, so it refuses an immediate repeat rather than every historical operation.

wording: One adapter action consumes 49,186 compute units and the four-action cohort totals 153,943, measured on real SBF execution rather than estimated.
limitations: Measured in LiteSVM, which is not an ephemeral rollup and not Devnet. A floor and a regression guard, not the Phase 3 budget.
Excludes commit overhead, committor overhead, and the ER-side scheduling cost, all of which Phase 3 must measure.
The four actions were executed as separate transactions here, not inside one Magic Action attempt.

wording: An adapter whose target CPI fails writes no receipt and consumes no capability nonce, so a reconciler can never mistake a failure for a delivered effect.
limitations: Covers a CPI that fails inside the target program. Phase 3 must observe what the committor does when a BaseAction fails inside a Magic Action attempt, which is a different failure mode.

wording: The VINCT core, sovereign adapter, and reference protocol programs are deployed and executable on Solana Devnet.
limitations: vinct_core on Devnet predates the D-0025 scheduling-order correction and needs an upgrade before a Devnet cohort can be scheduled.
Executability confirmed on both api.devnet.solana.com and rpc.magicblock.app/devnet. No VINCT instruction has been executed on Devnet yet.

wording: The MagicBlock devnet router returns the ephemeral rollup endpoint in getDelegationStatus for a genuinely delegated account, confirming the PRD's routing model.
limitations: Observed once, for one delegated account, on devnet. The response was {delegationRecord, fqdn, isDelegated} and resolved to https://devnet-as.magicblock.app/.
The client keeps a fallback chain because the local stack has no router at all.

wording: A four-action Magic Actions cohort delivered end to end on the local MagicBlock stack: three independent protocol markets paused and the settlement receipt was written.
limitations: Local stack, not Devnet. Says nothing about the Devnet committor.
Every effect was read back from base-layer account state; none was inferred from the ER scheduling signature.
The local stack required the committor program to be dumped from Devnet and preloaded; it is not shipped with the validator package.

wording: When one adapter action fails, the committor removes every BaseAction in the cohort and retries the commit alone, producing COMMIT_WITHOUT_ACTIONS rather than a partial application.
limitations: Local committor only. The Devnet committor is a separate deployment and this claim does not extend to it.
That all four actions shared one TransactionStrategy is inferred from all four disappearing together; the committor does not expose its grouping.
Only gamma's action was malformed. Alpha's and beta's were well-formed and still did not run, which is the substance of the finding.
A cohort large enough to split across strategies is untested.

wording: Every observed run returned a successful ER scheduling signature, including two in which no base-layer action ran at all.
limitations: This is the falsification of the naive settlement model, demonstrated rather than argued. It does not prove the classifier is correct for cases not yet observed.

wording: On Solana Devnet, one Magic Actions cohort paused three independently owned protocol markets and wrote the final settlement receipt, with every effect read back from base-layer account state.
limitations: Three reference protocols, not real deployed protocols. Each has an independent authority and its own registered adapter signer.
No effect was inferred from the ER scheduling signature; each was read from base-layer state.
Routed to the Europe ER because the Asia ER was serving a cached clone of the pre-upgrade program. See docs/decision-log.md D-0030.

wording: On Devnet, one failing adapter action caused the committor to remove every action in the cohort and retry the commit alone, producing COMMIT_WITHOUT_ACTIONS rather than a partial application.
limitations: Only gamma's action was malformed. Alpha's and beta's were well-formed and still did not run, which is the substance of the finding.
That all four actions shared one TransactionStrategy is inferred from all four disappearing together; the committor does not expose its grouping.
A cohort large enough to split across strategies remains untested. The reference bundle is four actions and fits one transaction.

wording: The Devnet cohort was measured, not estimated: 61,428 compute units for the ER scheduling transaction, 848 serialized bytes, 21 accounts, and 19.2 seconds from intent acceptance to every base-layer effect being observable.
limitations: The 280,000 CU across the four actions is the declared per-action budget, not consumed units. Per-action consumption inside a Magic Action attempt is not exposed by the committor.
The 19.2 second figure is one observation on one ER and is not a latency guarantee.
LiteSVM measured 49,854 CU for one adapter action directly, which remains the best per-action figure available.

wording: The rollup used for Phase 4 was selected by asking every router-advertised endpoint for a TDX quote over a fresh 64-byte challenge; one of four answered with a quote whose report data matched the challenge.
limitations: The check does not compare MRTD, RTMR, or configuration values against an expected workload allowlist, so it does not establish which code runs inside the enclave.
It establishes neither traffic-analysis resistance nor concealment of an incident’s existence.

wording: On the TEE-backed Devnet rollup, two members each mutated an account neither of them could read, and neither could read the other’s private account; the program’s arithmetic over all three was correct.
limitations: Established against one attested rollup on Devnet. It is behaviour of the current MagicBlock runtime, not a documented protocol guarantee, so it should be re-checked after a validator upgrade.

The probe program is a throwaway that models the shape of the question. The same property is exercised end to end by the Phase 4 runner, which is still blocked on that rollup’s stale executable cache.

wording: No account holds quorum progress while an incident is live, a member’s decision is written only to that member’s own account, and certification of two of three members does not wait for the third.
limitations: This is the half no rollup can do for us: that the program never puts a peer’s decision or a running tally where a peer could read it. Whether the rollup then enforces who may read which account needs a live PER, and that run is pending.

wording: A release with the claim and two of three ballots scrubbed is still refused with PrivateFieldsNotZeroized; every private account is checked on its own bytes before the flag.
limitations: The Devnet observation of the same gate is pending on the attested rollup refreshing its executable cache.

wording: On the local MagicBlock stack, a member reads their own ballot and is refused every other member’s; so are the opening responder, an authenticated outsider, and an anonymous caller. The claim is readable by members only, the public core by anyone, and the whole five-account lifecycle certifies, scrubs, and releases.
limitations: No enclave and no attestation. This establishes that the reference query-filtering service enforces the permission model as documented, not that a confidential runtime is holding the line. The TEE claim needs the Devnet run.
The local stack has no router, so endpoint resolution is configured rather than discovered.

wording: Certification proves it received the exact frozen ballot set rather than trusting the caller: eighteen adversarial mutations — missing, extra, duplicated, reordered, relabelled, foreign-incident, foreign-owner, wrong-version, scrubbed, and substituted-core — are each refused by a named error.
limitations: Where the frozen member list itself comes from is the covenant registry, which is Phase 5. Until then the opener supplies it, and certification proves only that the ballots match what was frozen at open.

wording: All 512 three-member cases agree with crates/vinct-reference: four choices per member, every quarantine subset, both sides of the deadline. The two implementations share no code.
limitations: Before the deadline the model may already call an incident rejected or impossible while the program still refuses to settle it. That difference is deliberate and is encoded in the test: the model is a view of the state, the program is a transition on it.

wording: Error code, public account state, submission acknowledgement, account lifecycle, emitted events, and compute units are each identical across incidents that differ only in how close they are to their threshold.
limitations: Constant-time execution is not claimed and not tested.
Resistance to an observer correlating transaction traffic is not claimed.
An incident’s existence, deadline, and member count are public by design.

wording: An incident’s member set, threshold, rejection ceiling, response window, policy, and epoch are copied from a covenant that every member ratified and every adapter-owning member armed. Opening takes no terms at all; its only argument is the digest of the claim.
limitations: The covenant is not yet deployed to Devnet: the program has outgrown its deployed capacity and the deployer balance cannot cover an extend plus the transient upgrade buffer. The Devnet gate for this is pending funding, not pending code.
The adapter capability recorded on a membership is not yet cross-checked against vinct_adapter’s own capability account. That binding is the next composition step.

wording: A certificate can only be produced by an incident that reached its covenant’s threshold. publish_certificate takes no arguments and no issuing authority: every field is derived from the released incident core, and its operation ID is the canonical derivation of the frozen snapshot, computed by the same function the reference model and the standalone verifier use.
limitations: The composition is proven up to the certificate. The Magic Action cohort beyond it still assumes a client-chosen operation ID, which Phase 5 no longer produces. See docs/decision-log.md D-0048.
Not yet run on Devnet: the program has outgrown its deployed capacity and the deployer is 1.76 SOL short of an extend plus the transient upgrade buffer.

wording: A protocol authority arms a versioned action template before any incident exists, and that one arming settles two separately certified incidents under the same covenant. Both certificates are earned by an incident reaching its threshold; neither is written by the test. Neither operation can consume the other's receipt, and a capability suspended after a certificate is issued still refuses to execute.
limitations: Proven in LiteSVM. The same capability serving two operations through two live Magic Action cohorts is not yet run on the local stack; the single-cohort live path is covered by phase5-composition-earns-its-own-certificate.

The reference model and the standalone verifier compute the template commitment from ActionTemplateV1; the adapter rebuilds it from its own fixed account list. They agree by construction and by test, not by sharing code, which is deliberate.

wording: The full sequence runs with nothing chosen by the runner: three protocols form and arm a covenant, an incident opens under it, collects a private claim and two sealed attestations inside a Private Ephemeral Rollup, certifies in memory, scrubs, and releases; the certificate is published permissionlessly from the released core; and the Magic Action cohort settles under the operation ID certification derived. Three markets pause, three adapter receipts are written, and the settlement receipt finalizes. Every effect is read from base-layer account state after the fact.
limitations: Local MagicBlock stack, not the TEE-backed Devnet PER. Confidentiality against the node operator is a separate rung and is claimed separately.
One cohort of three adapters plus a settlement receipt. Larger cohorts are bounded by the CU benchmarks, not by this run.

wording: A single BaseAction that cannot succeed removes the whole strategy: with one protocol's adapter signer unregistered, and again with one protocol's capability suspended after certification, no market paused, no adapter receipt was written, and the settlement receipt did not finalize. Both runs classify as COMMIT_WITHOUT_ACTIONS from observed base state, never from the scheduling signature.
limitations: Observed on the local stack with one strategy holding all four actions. A cohort split across several strategies would fail differently, and VINCT does not currently split one.
This is why recovery is a governed proposal under a new operation ID: the actions that appear to have run did not, so retrying the visible gap alone would leave the cohort half applied.

wording: Against certificates an incident earned rather than a test wrote: substituting any single account of the canonical bundle for the corresponding account of a different armed protocol is refused and the canonical bundle still executes; and a settled operation is refused a second execution by the adapter receipt, by the target protocol's own last_operation_id, and by the settlement receipt, with no state moved.
limitations: Account-level substitution from the set of armed protocols in the fixture. Arbitrary attacker-controlled accounts are covered separately in adversarial.rs against manufactured certificates, where forging is the point.

wording: The TypeScript settlement monitor reaches the same classification, status, and recovery eligibility as crates/vinct-types on all 729 observations of a two-action cohort, and all four classifications are reachable in that sweep. An RPC that hangs yields NotObserved and classifies as Unknown, never as CommitWithoutActions, proven by running the real observer against a server that accepts connections and never answers.
limitations: Two actions. Larger cohorts are covered by the same branches, and the sweep is exhaustive only at that width.
The delivery states Reverted and RemovedBeforeRetry are never assigned, because neither is visible in account state. Both need the base transaction's own log.

wording: A recovery proposal is only produced for CommitWithoutActions. PartialObservation and Unknown are refused outright, the missing action list is derived from the observations rather than supplied by the caller, the recovery draws a new operation ID that matches the Rust derivation, reusing the original certificate nonce is refused, and one original operation gets at most one recovery.
limitations: The registry is a client-side governance artifact. Nothing on chain enforces that a recovery was proposed before a new cohort is scheduled; what the chain enforces is that the new operation ID is different, which is what makes a duplicate effect impossible.

wording: When the router is reachable, publishes a routing table, and that table does not list the validator named in the account's delegation record, endpoint resolution returns no endpoint and the source router-mismatch. A configured endpoint is supplied in the test and is deliberately not substituted. A router that is unreachable, or one with an empty table, remains an absence of evidence and still falls back.
limitations: Against a stub router. The live devnet router's getDelegationStatus shape for a delegated account is still unconfirmed; see docs/decision-log.md D-0009.

wording: A standalone verifier re-derives the operation ID from the covenant's terms with an implementation sharing no code with the program, and confirms it equals the one the program recorded, the one the certificate carries, and the one every adapter and settlement receipt is bound to. It also confirms the incident's frozen snapshot is the covenant's terms, that the threshold that certified is the covenant's threshold, that the certificate was issued by the incident rather than by any authority, and that the private fields were zeroized before release. 17 checks, VERIFIED on all three local runs.
limitations: Verification is of operation identity, not of delivery. Delivery is reported alongside and explicitly not asserted, because a cohort that was scheduled and stripped has correctly bound receipts and no effects. See docs/decision-log.md D-0058.
The verifier uses the client's account decoders, which are themselves pinned to generated vectors. The operation-ID derivation shares no code with the program.

wording: Regenerating both vector files produces no diff against what is committed, so every cross-language parity test is checking the TypeScript against the layout the Rust defines today. This is a gate because it was once false: ActionTemplateV1 gained six fields and the vectors were never regenerated, so the vectors and the TypeScript agreed with each other and neither agreed with the program.
limitations: Catches drift between the Rust definitions and the committed vectors. It cannot catch a Rust definition that is itself wrong.

wording: The Phase 5 gate's named failure cases each have a test: a covenant past its epoch window cannot host a new incident and one that never armed cannot either; a member cannot be added or substituted after ratification freezes the set; an unarmed capability refuses a valid certificate; a quarantined member cannot attest; an expired certificate is refused; a mutated bundle is refused against an earned certificate; a router that contradicts the delegation record resolves nothing; and a service that hangs classifies as Unknown.
limitations: Router mismatch and service timeout are proven against stubs rather than a degraded live service, which is the honest rung for a failure you cannot ask a provider to produce on demand.

wording: An incident that nobody answers reaches a terminal status without any human acting. A task requested on the rollup was registered and executed by the scheduler, its early iterations did nothing while the response window was open, and the iteration after the deadline settled the incident to EXPIRED. The private accounts were then scrubbed, the permissions closed, and the family released to base with the scrub verified there.
limitations: Local MagicBlock stack. Scheduler behaviour on the TEE-backed Devnet rollup is unverified.
A requested iteration count is not a delivered one, and nothing in the design depends on it. See docs/decision-log.md D-0059.

wording: The scheduled handler does nothing before the deadline and does nothing after the incident is terminal, returning success in both cases so a scheduler does not retry work that is finished. Four iterations after settlement leave the incident's bytes unchanged, including the operation ID and the certification slot. It performs whatever terminal transition the tally implies, through the same function the manual path uses, so a crank-settled incident and a manually-settled one reach the same status.
limitations: LiteSVM has no scheduler. What is proven is VINCT behaving correctly when called, not that the scheduler calls it; that is the live-stack claim.

wording: An incident's task ID is a domain-separated digest of the cluster, the covenant, and the incident, with the sign bit cleared. Two incidents under one covenant derive different IDs, forty consecutive incidents all derive positive ones, and the derivation is recomputed independently in the test rather than read from the program.
limitations: Collision resistance rests on SHA-256 truncated to 63 bits. That is a birthday bound around 3 billion tasks per scheduler instance, which is far beyond any covenant's incident count but is not the full digest.

wording: The scheduler takes the signer of a schedule request as the task's authority and silently drops a cancel from any other key. VINCT therefore requires the incident's opener to sign both. A stranger and a co-member are each refused with IncidentWrongOpener at the program, and a corrected live run cancels after 7 of 32 iterations and the task stops.
limitations: Removal is established by absence over a quiet window with exhaustion excluded, because this validator exposes no task registry. See docs/decision-log.md D-0061 and D-0063.

wording: VINCT cannot undelegate an incident that is still collecting, because release_incident requires a terminal status. In the remaining window, a finite task with iterations left after its accounts were released, 11 further iterations fired and all 11 failed with AccountOwnedByWrongProgram and InvalidWritableAccount. Both refusals come from the runtime and Anchor's account checks before any VINCT code runs. The incident stayed EXPIRED on base and the scrub still verified.
limitations: Measured for one release. The failure mode is a property of the runtime's account checks rather than of VINCT, so it should be re-measured on any validator whose delegation semantics differ.

wording: The pinned validator's own logs say request, for both scheduling and cancellation. Every state after REQUESTED and CANCELLATION_REQUESTED is read from the rollup: iterations from transactions where the crank executor ran and left its completion marker, the desired state from the incident account, and removal from absence over a quiet window with exhaustion excluded. Registration is inferred from an observed execution, which under-reports and never over-reports.
limitations: This validator exposes no task registry, so REGISTRATION_OBSERVED cannot be established directly. The weakening is one-way and recorded in docs/decision-log.md D-0063.

wording: Walking every route of the built bundle, the browser persists exactly one storage key, holding a covenant address, which is public on chain. Nothing resembling a claim, a decision, a nonce, or a signature reaches storage. The app contacts its own origin and the RPC endpoints named in the URL and no other host, carries no analytics global, and loads no script from a CDN.
limitations: Asserted against the built bundle on desktop and mobile Chromium. A different engine could in principle differ, though none of these properties is engine-specific.

wording: A deep link carrying an operation ID verifies it with no wallet, no login, and no signature: the page reads the incident and its covenant from the chain, re-derives the operation ID with an implementation that shares no code with the program, and renders every check separately. Timed under the gate's two minutes. Delivery is reported next to the verdict and explicitly not folded into it.
limitations: The operation must exist on the cluster the link names. The page says which cluster it looked at when it does not, rather than reporting a failed verification.

wording: The same 15 assertions pass on Desktop Chrome and on a Pixel 7 viewport: every route loads and keeps the selected covenant, a missing route explains that nothing is being withheld, a deep link survives a reload, an unreachable node renders as an outage rather than an empty result, and the status page names what stops working for each service that is down.
limitations: Two viewports. The mobile project found two bugs where a control stayed visible and stopped being clickable, so the coverage is load-bearing rather than decorative. See docs/decision-log.md D-0068.

wording: The public incident view renders no approval count while an incident is collecting, and says why: no account holds it. The count exists only as a number the program computes in memory during certification. The incident room shows which private accounts exist and their state, never their contents, and states that it holds no member key and opens no authenticated rollup connection.
limitations: The page cannot leak what it cannot read, which is a property of the account model rather than of the page. The browser assertion is a regression guard on the wording and the absence, not the proof of the privacy claim; that is the PER experiment.
